summary: Addressed 34 critic issues (2 blockers, 15 majors, 17 minors); 30 resolved with new or corrected evidence, 4 partly resolved and carried as open questions. New idle benchmarks: real-stack single-change variants (copy.copy removed alone: 58.84/58.98 fps vs 54.14 HEAD), P8 with lockstep + metadata (59.82/59.95 fps), P3 asymmetric stall (block+lockstep keeps sync; drop/no-lockstep desyncs by 606-639 ms), P11 crash containers (killed MSMF .mp4 0/300 readable), P12 physical disk, P10 threads=1 unthrottled, deflate on real payloads, P6 repeats. recommend_result.json was rewritten (new rank 2; ranks renumbered with previous_rank) and the stage READMEs corrected.

open_questions: Real 5 x 60 fps capture: none of the 4 attached UVC cameras delivered more than 30.1 fps (p9_real_camera.md). USB host-controller bandwidth with 5 real cameras is unmeasured.

Lockstep (or a group commit) is kept for recording (P3 ASYM). Open: whether non-recording consumers could group free-running frames by timestamp instead, and what sync quality that gives on real cameras.
Whether DSHOW decodes MJPEG on the calling thread or a graph thread, and therefore which e2e stand-in (mjpeg 53.6 fps or memcpy 59.99 fps) a real camera resembles.

Spill-to-disk as a full-ring policy was not tested. Raw write-through with the SLC cache exhausted was (P12: 481-1508 MB/s, 5 paced streams kept 162 MB/s, worst write 138 ms); recorder behaviour through the real encoders on a slow or nearly full disk was not.
Whether MSMF H.264 runs on the GPU or in software on this machine, and why the thread-pool setting changes its CPU 3x (inferred busy-waiting, not profiled).
Whether FreeMoCap's posthoc pipeline accepts MJPEG-in-MKV recordings (rank 8). FreeMoCap realtime-pipeline contention at 5x60 fps was not measured.
The memory-ordering guarantee of the numpy seqlock on non-x86 CPUs. There were 0 torn frames in 50 SPSC runs on x86, which is evidence, not proof.
Browser-side UI throughput (no browser was attached in P6 or d_ui).
Accuracy of the accumulated-clock drop detector (rank 5) on real DSHOW cameras; on the synthetic stack it matched the true count within +5 (e2ev_gap_detector.md).
Per-frame capture-thread CPU of real cameras at 60 fps (P9 measured 11.0-14.7 ms per 1080p frame at 30 fps as a process total; the P8 lockstep design loses about 2 fps with 3 ms more CPU).

Antivirus (Defender real-time scan) and GC pauses as recorder stalls during a 10-minute 5x1080p60 recording through the real encoders; P12 measured raw write-through stalls only (no encoder, Defender in its default state).
NVENC session-exhaustion and mid-recording driver-reset handling (rank 14) and the rank-1 fault-injection test were specified but not built.
Whether FreeMoCap's posthoc reader accepts MKV / fragmented MP4 recordings (rank 2) and tolerates a truncated last fragment.
A packed variable-size compressed ring (rank 8's ~154 s per GiB estimate) was not built; the built prototype holds 17 s.
Hybrid CPU (8 P-cores + 12 E-cores): no run pinned affinity or recorded core-type placement; the idle rule is a share of all 28 logical CPUs. Part of the run-to-run variance may come from placement.

Real-camera hardware sync: with free-running cameras the capture-time spread of a multiframe is set by the sensors' phases (7-13 ms median, up to 20 ms on the synthetic stack) whatever the software does; whether the target cameras support a sync input was not examined.
